page: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. The host is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a dedicated 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware security and instruction set support include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, but exclude AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance provides a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and includes no local bundled storage or discrete GPU accelerators, requiring external network block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark analysis highlights robust multi-threaded computational capabilities alongside distinct single-thread limitations. The instance achieves strong scores in PassMark CPU tests, including PassMark CPU encryption ranking in the top 10% (102,373.82) and overall CPU score in the top 25% (69,068.55). High-concurrency operations also perform well, evidenced by Geekbench software compilation (42,782.0) and ray tracing (77,168.0), as well as 83.89 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core metrics represent a tradeoff: stress-ng single-core performance registers in the bottom 10% (749.38), and Geekbench single-core lands in the middle 50% (1,321.0), showing that raw per-thread latency is subordinate to massive parallel throughput.

In terms of memory and specialized execution, cached 16 KB read memory bandwidth is strong at 4,497.3 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB reads reach 119.53 GB/sec and writes reach 60.96 GB/sec. Large language model inference yields mixed results without hardware acceleration: prompt processing for a small 135M parameter model is strong at 3,018.89 tokens/sec, but degrades to 15.2 tokens/sec for 70B models, with text generation reaching 2.91 tokens/sec on 70B models. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from its high density of 96 dedicated threads on AMD silicon, favoring scalable horizontal compute tasks over workloads requiring fast single-thread response or heavy AVX-512 vectorization.

The AWS c5a.24xlarge is best suited for parallelized compute tasks, such as distributed CI/CD build farms, batch processing, ray tracing, web service fleets, and in-memory key-value caching such as Redis. It is less optimal for single-threaded processing pipelines, AVX-512 accelerated numerical simulations, or large local storage workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based server featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs at 3.3 GHz, and 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 20 Gbps baseline network throughput, zero local storage, and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional multi-threaded performance, including top-tier encryption execution and strong scores in PassMark CPU, software compilation, and Redis key-value operations. However, stress-ng single-core output ranks in the bottom 10%, reflecting lower single-thread throughput. Lacking AVX-512 extensions and local disks, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for high-density parallel workloads rather than per-core speed. The c5a.24xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, batch data processing, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving tiers.
